contraindications: Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin or other anticoagulants within 24 hours of IV alteplase: additive bleeding risk; withhold until 24 hours and follow-up brain imaging without hemorrhage.
interactions: Levetiracetam + alteplase, lisinopril, metformin or atorvastatin: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic or hemostatic interaction; renally cleared, dose by creatinine clearance.
Valproate + alteplase or antiplatelet agents: dose-related thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction add to bleeding risk; avoid in the first days after thrombolysis.
Fosphenytoin or phenytoin + atorvastatin: CYP3A4 induction lowers atorvastatin exposure; enzyme induction also complicates later anticoagulant dosing.
Lacosamide + other PR-prolonging drugs: additive PR prolongation; obtain an ECG before loading.
Lisinopril + alteplase: ACE inhibition increases the risk of orolingual angioedema during and after the infusion; inspect the tongue and lips.
Metformin + iodinated contrast: withhold metformin after contrast when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or in acute kidney injury.
output.proposed: Levetiracetam, valproate, fosphenytoin or lacosamide with lisinopril, metformin and atorvastatin, after IV alteplase

output.query: Periodic discharges and seizures after acute ischemic stroke and reperfusion therapy

results.finding: Periodic discharges averaging above 1 Hz and up to 2.5 Hz, or 0.5 to 1 Hz with a plus modifier or fluctuation, that do not meet criteria for electrographic seizures are classified on the ictal-interictal continuum.

Discharges at 2.5 Hz or less qualify as non-convulsive status epilepticus only with typical spatiotemporal evolution, subtle ictal clinical phenomena, or clinical and EEG improvement after IV antiseizure medication.
Continuous EEG for at least 24 hours is recommended when non-convulsive seizures are suspected in patients with acute brain injury and impaired consciousness.
Seizures after acute ischemic stroke are treated as in other acute neurological conditions; prophylactic antiseizure medication is not recommended.

output.summary: Periodic discharges without evolution are classified on the ictal-interictal continuum [ACNS_2021], and slow periodic patterns meet non-convulsive status epilepticus criteria only with evolution, ictal clinical correlates or a response to IV antiseizure medication [Salzburg_NCSE_2015]. Continuous EEG for at least 24 hours is recommended after acute brain injury with impaired consciousness [Brophy_2012]. Post-stroke seizures are treated as in other acute neurological conditions, without prophylaxis in patients who have not had a seizure [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose 192 mg/dL with HbA1c 8.4%; platelets 224 x10^9/L; INR 1.1, aPTT 31 s, fibrinogen 280 mg/dL; sodium, calcium, magnesium, renal and hepatic function normal: no metabolic cause of the seizures

action_criteria.rationale: Glucose, electrolyte, renal and hepatic derangements are reversible causes of seizures and decide the ASM and its dose; coagulation and fibrinogen because she received IV alteplase and underwent thrombectomy within the last 3 hours [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.rationale: Atrial fibrillation would change secondary prevention, and a baseline ECG precedes lacosamide or fosphenytoin [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not escalate to anaesthetic infusion or intubation to suppress LPDs without electrographic seizures.
Do not start antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy within 24 hours of alteplase.
Do not give valproate in the first days after thrombolysis when levetiracetam is available.
required_recommendations: Start a non-sedating ASM for the acute symptomatic seizure and the LPDs+F: IV levetiracetam load (20 to 60 mg/kg, maximum 4500 mg); prefer it to valproate, whose thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction add to bleeding risk after alteplase [Brophy_2012].
Continue video-EEG for at least 24 hours to detect evolution of the periodic discharges into electrographic seizures [Brophy_2012].

Lower the blood pressure (188/112) to 180/105 mmHg or below with IV labetalol or nicardipine and keep it there for 24 hours after alteplase and thrombectomy, without lowering systolic pressure below 140 mmHg after successful reperfusion [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].
Treat hyperglycemia (glucose 192 mg/dL) with insulin to a target of 140 to 180 mg/dL [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].

Withhold antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy until 24 hours after alteplase and follow-up brain imaging without hemorrhage, then start antiplatelet therapy and a high-intensity statin [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].
Neuro-ICU or stroke unit care with frequent neurological checks and continuous cardiac monitoring for at least 24 hours; repeat urgent CT for any further neurological decline [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].

avoided_actions.rationale: A neuropsychological battery cannot be performed in an aphasic, drowsy patient and has no acute role.
LP is not indicated: the seizures are explained by the acute infarct, there is no infectious or autoimmune suspicion, and a puncture within hours of alteplase risks spinal hematoma.

accepted: Acute left MCA ischemic stroke with post-ischemic lateralized periodic discharges on ictal-interictal continuum and post-reperfusion seizures

differential.diagnosis: Non-convulsive status epilepticus (electrographic seizures meeting Salzburg criteria)
differential.key_features: The continuous EEG shows LPDs+F at 1.5-2 Hz without evolution, no electrographic seizures, and the arm episodes have no EEG correlate; NCSE remains possible on longer monitoring, hence cEEG for 24 hours

differential.diagnosis: Hemorrhagic transformation after alteplase and thrombectomy
differential.key_features: Worsening after reperfusion therapy raises it, but CT shows no hemorrhage and SWI no susceptibility signal loss; coagulation and fibrinogen normal

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral hyperperfusion or reperfusion edema after recanalization
differential.key_features: BP 188/112 after recanalization; imaging shows only mild sulcal effacement within the infarct and no hemorrhage
BP 188/112, but the diffusion restriction is territorial in the left MCA and there is no posterior vasogenic edema
A seizure occurred during the infusion, but CTA showed a left M1 occlusion and MRI an acute DWI infarct in that territory

key_clinical_evidence: Periodic discharges averaging above 1 Hz and up to 2.5 Hz without evolution lie on the ictal-interictal continuum [ACNS_2021]; slower discharges meet NCSE criteria only with evolution, subtle ictal phenomena or a response to IV ASM [Salzburg_NCSE_2015].
Paroxysmal limb stiffening without an EEG correlate is not an electrographic seizure; video-EEG separates the two.

A 30-second episode of rhythmic limb jerking during thrombolysis is an acute symptomatic seizure, not cortical spreading depression, and warrants an ASM; prophylaxis without a seizure is not recommended [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].
After IV alteplase and thrombectomy, blood pressure is kept at 180/105 mmHg or below for 24 hours and antithrombotics wait 24 hours for imaging without hemorrhage [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].
Hyperglycemia worsens stroke outcome; the target is 140 to 180 mg/dL [AHA_ASA_Stroke_2026].

patient.chief_complaint: Worsening confusion and brief episodes of right arm stiffening 90 minutes after thrombectomy for a left MCA stroke

family_history: Mother: hypertension, stroke at 62. Father: diabetes. No family history of epilepsy.

medications.frequency: single IV infusion started at 10:05 at the outside hospital, about 3 hours before this evaluation

social_history.note: Social worker. Single, lives alone. Non-smoker. Rare alcohol. No illicit drugs. Poorly medication-adherent per chart notes.

patient.history_present_illness: A 44-year-old right-handed Black woman, a social worker with poorly controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes, was found by a coworker at 09:10 with right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking; she had been seen well at 08:30. At the community hospital the NIHSS was 14, with leftward gaze deviation, right facial droop, right hemiparesis and nonfluent aphasia. Non-contrast CT showed no hemorrhage and CTA showed a left M1 occlusion; IV alteplase was started at 10:05. During the infusion she had a 30-second episode of rhythmic jerking of the right arm, which the outside team attributed to post-ischemic cortical spreading depression; no antiseizure medication was given. She was transferred to your center, where mechanical thrombectomy completed at 11:40 achieved near-complete reperfusion of the left MCA territory (TICI 2b) after one pass. On return to the neuro-ICU she was more alert, with an NIHSS of 8. About 90 minutes after the procedure the nurse noted that she had become more confused, with brief episodes of stiff flexion of the right arm several times an hour and a persistent leftward gaze preference. The team is unsure whether the arm episodes are seizures and how aggressively to treat them so soon after alteplase.
